newsitem.title: SPAIN: N.Ireland, Spain share street violence experiences.
newsitem.headline: N.Ireland, Spain share street violence experiences.

text.p: Northern Ireland minister Michael Ancram said on Thursday street violence was a growing problem that Northern Ireland and Spain shared and that each could learn from the other's experiences.

During a two-day visit to Spain, Ancram visited the Basque country, home to Basque separatist group ETA which is fighting for independence from Spain, and met Spanish Foreign Minister Jaime Mayor Oreja.
"The real area of shared concern that I came across is the use of very young people in these street violence incidents," he told journalists.
"(It) is building a sub-culture of violence for the future and we identified this as an area where there is work to be done," he added.
Street violence has risen in Spain over the past six months particularly in the Basque region, where gangs of hooded youths use fire bombs to destroy public property.
In a crackdown on such violence, Spanish police on Thursday arrested 18 more people allegedly affiliated to youth groups with links to ETA (Basque Homeland and Freedom).

"Over the summer we have (also) had a vast amount of experience in street violence and the ways we are trying to combat that through the communities, through the schools is something we can share," Ancram said.
